graphEvents.label: Does the council use the same executor dispatch?
Which extensions remove the defects found?
Council external-cli has no dispatch runtime

label: deep-review-auto.yaml acquires the packet lock without --owner-pid, so loop-lock.cjs marks it owner_kind transient and loop-lock.ts skips the dead-owner probe for that kind: a killed review run blocks the packet for 2 x TTL (60 min) instead of being reclaimable, and the step note's 'owning process is known to be dead' staleness clause is unreachable from this invocation. The research variant shares the omission.

deep-review-auto.yaml's if_cli_opencode repeats all four research argv defects: unguarded '{config.executor.model}' at 1434 (five later branches use the null guard), v1-only '--pure' at 1547, literal command 'opencode' at 1570 so OPENCODE_BIN and the installed major are ignored. The seam is one defect in two files, not two slips.

The council's external-cli mode is a prompt contract with no dispatch runtime: no council asset contains if_cli_* or runAuditedExecutorCommand, and dispatchCouncilSeats requires an injected dispatchSeat that no non-test file supplies. It inherits none of the research/review argv defects and none of their protections; --executor TYPE binds a value the runtime never reads.

summarizeSnapshots returns only {total, succeeded, failed, all_failed}; there is no field in which a caller can quote a failure reason, so 'a failed run says why it failed' holds per lineage event but not in the aggregate the workflow step reads.

Extension: export one argv builder (resolveOpencodeBinary + per-kind assembly) from fanout-run.cjs and have the single-executor branches in deep-research-auto.yaml and deep-review-auto.yaml consume it. Without it, five defects share one cause across four call sites.

Extension: give convergence.cjs a --config-json owner for stopPolicy and minIterations. Neither convergence.cjs nor reduce-state.cjs mentions either key today, so the stop rule is asserted in JSON, restated in YAML prose and never enforced by the script that computes convergence.

Extension: emit a typed executor_switch event (abandoned kind + reason) with a per-kind switch target list, so a devin resource_exhausted or an unavailable binary migrates instead of terminating; the executor is currently bound once at config load and the council has no binding at all.
A lock that a short-lived CLI process acquires is reclaimable only by heartbeat age; any workflow that wants dead-owner reclaim must pass --owner-pid.

direction: Council shares the research/review if_cli_* argv defects
reason: No council asset contains an if_cli_* branch or a runAuditedExecutorCommand call; seats are dispatched through a caller-injected dispatchSeat that no production file supplies.

direction: Missing --runtime-kind in the acquire command is a second lock bug
reason: loop-lock.cjs defaults runtimeKind to 'main' when the flag is absent, so the omission is benign.
